description:
Factory AI GMO's commercial platform needs a way for an Organization to create and manage Projects -- the container under which Factory Runs (invocations of the Software Construction Factory) will later be recorded, along with their generated Artifacts, Usage, and Billing. This is the third module in the dependency chain (Account -> Organization -> Projects -> Factory Runs -> Artifacts -> Usage -> Billing) and continues the same two-factory architecture already established: the Software Factory constructs software; a separate Commercial Factory (not yet built) will later turn that software into customers and revenue.

BUSINESS REQUIREMENTS
- An authenticated member of an Organization can create a new Project within that Organization.
- A Project has a human-readable name and a short description of what it represents, since a customer will accumulate multiple Projects over time and needs to tell them apart.
- A Project has a lifecycle status, since a customer will need to archive Projects no longer in active use without deleting their history.
- Authorized members of the owning Organization can view, list, and update a Project's own details. Exactly which members can do so is not decided here (see Open Question #2).
- This module does not yet cover creating or running a Factory Run against a Project, or storing any generated artifact, validation result, usage record, or billing event -- those are separate, later modules in the dependency chain and must not be invented here.

CONSTRAINTS -- already decided, satisfy them rather than re-deciding them
- A Project is not a POS GMO retail-platform concept and must never be given a companyId, for the same reason `organization` must not: it belongs to Factory AI GMO's own commercial-platform tenancy model, not POS GMO's retail tenancy model. It has no existing companyId relationship to POS GMO's own `companies` table.
- A Project belongs to exactly one Organization. However, `organization` (tests/prd_organization.json) has itself only reached the same construction-reliability state as `factoryAccount`: validated as a design (a clean, fully-compliant backend/frontend pass) but not yet applied to a live repository, so no `organizations` table exists live to formally reference. Model the owning Organization as a plain reference field (see `organizationSlug`), not a foreign key -- the same reasoning `organization` itself used for `ownerEmail` against `factoryAccount`. Do not invent an `organizations` table as a side effect of this PRD, and do not silently substitute any POS GMO table for it.
- created_At/updated_at remain server-controlled, same convention as every other module in this repository.

OPEN ARCHITECTURAL QUESTIONS -- deliberately unresolved; do not silently pick an answer and hide the ambiguity
1. Formal ownership relationship: this PRD deliberately does not declare a foreign key to `organizations` because that table isn't live yet. If/when it is, converting `organizationSlug` into a real relationship is a natural follow-up, not something to force here.
2. Membership/permission model: which members of an Organization (owner only, any member, or a role within the Organization) can create, view, or archive its Projects is not decided. This platform's own role vocabulary for its authenticated side is itself an open question already recorded in `organization`'s PRD (Open Question #2) and is not re-decided here.
3. Slug uniqueness scope: whether a Project's slug must be unique globally or only within its owning Organization is not specified -- an open design question for the Architect/Database agents, the same way `organization`'s own slug-generation question was left open.
4. Relationship to Factory Runs: this PRD does not define what a Factory Run is, how it is triggered, or how it relates to a Project beyond "a Project is the container it will belong to" -- that is the next module in the dependency chain and must not be invented here.

This PRD intentionally leaves architecture decisions (schema shape, relationships, endpoints beyond standard CRUD) to the Architect/Database/Backend agents, consistent with the commercialization plan's own instruction that 'the exact modules and schema should be discovered and designed by the Software Factory from the commercial requirements rather than assumed in advance.'

fields.name: name
fields.description: Human-readable Project name, e.g. 'Q4 POS Rollout'.

fields.name: slug
fields.description: URL-safe handle for this Project, used in the commercial platform's own URLs. Uniqueness scope (global vs. within its Organization) is an open design question -- see description.

fields.name: organizationSlug
fields.description: Slug of the owning Organization (see tests/prd_organization.json). A plain field, not a foreign key, because `organizations` does not yet exist in the live database -- see Open Architectural Question #1.

fields.name: description
fields.description: Free-text description of what this Project represents or is for.

fields.name: status
fields.description: Project lifecycle state, e.g. active, archived. Defaults to active on creation. Transition rules are an open design question, not specified here.
